title: On-prem/VPC observability: resilient sidecar for trace propagation and scoped buffering
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a lightweight, tenant-aware sidecar for Dedicated and Private deployments that guarantees trace context propagation, local buffering under collector outages, and deterministic failover to perimeter relays. This ticket covers the sidecar behaviour, protocol compatibility (W3C traceparent + Redwood envelope), scoped disk/ram quotas per tenant, backpressure signals for request routing, and metrics/logging for SLO dashboards.
background: Customers running Redwood Private and Dedicated have asked for stronger guarantees when on-prem collectors or VPC relays are temporarily unreachable. Current behavior drops spans or returns opaque 5xx when the perimeter layer is saturated. We need a focused sidecar that can preserve trace continuity for a bounded window, expose clear signals to the runtime for graceful degradation, and instrument the failure modes so console dashboards can show precise latency/error attribution by tenant and path.
acceptance_criteria: Sidecar reliably propagates W3C traceparent and Redwood trace-envelopes to downstream services without modifying application headers
When collector is unavailable, sidecar buffers up to configured per-tenant disk quota (default 100MB) and exposes LIFO drop policy and watermark metrics
Sidecar emits standardized backpressure metric and header (x-rd-backpressure: low|med|high) usable by router to reroute to fallback relay
E2E test harness reproduces collector outage and validates zero-trace-loss for 95% of spans within 30s buffer window under normal load
Console dashboard shows: buffer fill %, per-tenant dropped spans count, end-to-end trace latency delta across failover, and a time-correlated outage annotation
design_decisions: Keep sidecar in Go to match existing collector runtime and minimize memory overhead
Use append-only local segment files for buffering to simplify crash recovery rather than a full embedded DB
Expose backpressure as both metrics (prom) and a downstream request header so routing logic can make fast decisions
Buffering is tenant-scoped; sidecar enforces per-tenant quotas to avoid noisy-tenant starvation
Failover strategy: prefer soft reroute to regional relay when backpressure==high, otherwise queue locally; only drop when both queue and relay are saturated
technical_notes: Buffer format: framed Redwood envelope (len-prefixed) with CRC32 and traceroot for fast indexing
Recovery: on restart, sidecar replays oldest segments first up to watermark, updates 'replay-offset' counter metric
Backpressure heuristic: moving-average of send success latency and consecutive 5xx ratio -> low/med/high thresholds configurable via JSON policy
Auth: sidecar uses customer KMS token to sign envelopes in private deployments; signing key rotation handled via local keycache
Resource limits: config knobs for max-memory-bytes, max-disk-bytes, per-tenant-max-disk, keep-alive interval for relay handshakes
tasks: Integration: router header handling + policy - Lena (ENG)
E2E tests: chaos harness for collector outages - QA team (Sandeep)

Docs: onprem deployment guide, config reference, and incident runbook - Docs (Claire)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: disk-buffer can become attack surface for data exfiltration in misconfigured instances -> Mitigation: encrypt files at rest with tenant-specific keys and enforce ACLs
Risk: sidecar CPU pressure under heavy replay -> Mitigation: rate-limit replay and provide token-bucket throttles and soft-fallback to relay
Risk: inconsistent trace ordering after replay -> Mitigation: annotate replayed spans with replay-timestamp and mark in dashboards so downstream evals can ignore replay noise

notes_for_reviewers: Please evaluate the trade-off between append-only file segments vs LevelDB for local index speed. LevelDB reduces replay latency but increases code surface and embedded dependencies.
Suggest reviewing the backpressure thresholds in runtime config; current defaults are conservative and may cause premature reroute in high-latency networks.
Security: confirm KMS signing workflow is compatible with customer-managed keys in air-gapped installs
